**Final**

My project analyzes shot characteristics across multiple National Basketball Association (NBA) seasons and trains a model to predict the outcome of a shot. The goal is to explore how shot quality correlates with scoring and winning. I chose this topic because I love math and computer science, and I also play basketball as a hobby, so it seemed exciting to combine all three.

Collecting the data was challenging, and extending the analysis to additional seasons will require a lot of time. I also anticipate that writing the paper will be difficult, since I have never done this before.

The [dataset](https://www.nbasavant.com/shot_search.php) (from NBA Savant) has detailed shot characteristics from many past NBA seasons. A few example columns are the type of shot, distance, and time left on the clock. It also contains a binary indicator of whether the shot was made.

I use multiple models and choose the most accurate one. These include logistic regression, kNN, neural networks, random forest, gradient boosting, and catboost. 

 We then use this model to calculate a player and a team's expected points. Then we use a Z-test to see if there is a significant difference from the actual points scored. We then use the Pythagorean winning percentage to predict wins and compare them to the actual result. This will reflect the team's true “skill” better than the result. If I finish early, I can extend this into classifying player archetypes.

I want to target many journals, but my main focus will be the Wharton Sports Analytics Journal.
